findings.summary: (Fixed in the prior round, re-confirmed unaffected by this round's changes.) Meeting deletion takes EntityResolver.lockUserGraph before the meeting row lock, closing the resolve/delete race. Re-read: nothing in this round's diff touches this file.
(Fixed in the prior round, re-confirmed.) meetingGraph's node query filters e.user_id.

New this round: normalizeEntityName now strips a leading category word per type ('công ty', 'ngân hàng', 'khách hàng' for organization; 'dự án' for project; 'ứng dụng' etc. for product) before the name enters tier-1 exact matching. This is the right fix for the live-check false-negative (28 entities → 25, the 9 expected each found exactly once), but it also raises tier 1's collision surface: two genuinely different organizations that happen to share a bare/prefixed name within the same type (e.g. a real 'Ngân hàng ABC' and an unrelated 'Công ty ABC', both normalizing to 'abc' under type=organization) would now auto-join at tier 1 with no suggestion step and no chance for the user to review, since tier 1 auto-attaches. This mirrors the honorific-stripping precedent for PERSON (already accepted) but the collision base rate for common category+short-name combinations in Vietnamese business speech (many small vendors/banks named after a person or place) is plausibly higher than for people's given names. No test exercises this collision; not caught by graph-live-check.mjs's synthetic transcript (each org name is unique there). Recommend a follow-up test asserting two distinct orgs that both reduce to the same normalized_name after category stripping are NOT silently the same entity if introduced with distinguishing descriptions, or documenting the trade-off explicitly as accepted (as was done for the search-precision trade-off in the live-check report's 'Remaining' section).
(Fixed in the prior round, re-confirmed.) Suggestions query now requires a.type = b.type at read time.
(Fixed in the prior round, re-confirmed.) A search string with no letters/digits now returns an empty page instead of matching everything.

Search precision can degrade for a query that types a category word plus a very short remainder (e.g. a 2-3 letter name): the needle computed under the matching type strips the prefix down to a short substring, which the OR'd LIKE '%...%' then matches broadly across unrelated entities of that type. Documented as an accepted, known trade-off in the live-check report's 'Remaining' section (opposite direction: typing only the category word no longer finds anything). Not a correctness or security issue — a precision/UX note only.

(Carried over, unaddressed this round.) The relation-matching find() re-normalizes each candidate entity's name per call instead of reusing the 'known' map already built during entity parsing. No correctness issue.
